title: Multi-symbol backtests report Sharpe understated by sqrt(N) and annualised return understated by ~N — the equity curve is sampled per BAR, the metrics assume per DAY
repro: sidecar/.venv/bin/python, in-process with a fixture bar_loader (no network): register a buy-and-hold strategy, feed a seeded random walk of 200 dates for N symbols, run backtest_engine.run_backtest. N=1: 200 curve points, sharpe 0.647, date-sampled sharpe 0.647 (ratio 1.00). N=2: 400 points, sharpe 0.674 vs 0.938 (ratio 1.39, sqrt2=1.41). N=4: 800 points, sharpe 1.087 vs 2.215 (ratio 2.04, sqrt4=2.00). annualizedReturn for N=4 reported +0.0023 where (1+totalReturn)^(252/200)-1 = +0.0090. Calmar derives from annualizedReturn so it inherits the error.
evidence: sidecar/services/backtest_engine.py:391 (equity_curve.append inside `for bar in bars` at :313), sidecar/services/backtest_engine.py:251-267 (returns built from consecutive curve points; sqrt(252) and **252 applied as if daily), sidecar/services/backtest_engine.py:434 (bars sorted by (timestamp, symbol) so N points share each date), src/modules/backtest/BacktestResultView.tsx:477-502 (all six numbers rendered), sidecar/services/agent_tools/backtest_summary.py:55 (same metrics fed to the Strategy Critic)
notes: Information leakage (APOSD 4): the metric function silently depends on the caller's sampling rate, which it cannot see. Multi-symbol is a first-class input — the panel field is literally 'Symbols (comma-sep)' (src/modules/backtest/BacktestPanel.tsx:196) and bar_loader fans out 8-wide. Consequence: Sharpe/Sortino/Calmar/annualizedReturn shown as fact and reasoned over by the Critic agent are wrong by a fixed factor the user has no way to detect. Smallest fix: collapse the curve to the last point per `timestamp` before _compute_metrics, or pass an explicit periods_per_year = len(returns)/dates_spanned instead of the literal 252.

refuter.reason: Confirmed: _run_single_slice appends one equity point per bar (not per date), and _compute_metrics treats consecutive points as daily returns with sqrt(252)/**252, so N-symbol runs understate Sharpe by ~sqrt(N) and annualised return (and Calmar) by ~N. Backtesting is historical strategy research, not order placement/paper brokerage, so the 23 Sep trading removal does not touch it.

title: `sortino` is not the Sortino ratio — the denominator is the stdev of the loss subset, measured 41x overstatement on a plausible return series
repro: sidecar/.venv/bin/python -c: build an equity curve from returns [+0.02]*10 + [-0.05, -0.051], call services.backtest_engine._compute_metrics(curve, [], 100000.0) -> metrics.sortino = 261.93. Textbook Sortino with downside deviation sqrt(mean(min(r,0)^2)) over all periods = 6.35. Overstated 41.2x. Degenerate case: two identical losses -> pstdev == 0 -> the `if downside_stdev > 0` guard returns sortino = 0.00, visually identical to 'no downside'.
evidence: sidecar/services/backtest_engine.py:259-260 (`downside = [r for r in returns if r < 0]`; `downside_stdev = statistics.pstdev(downside)`), sidecar/services/backtest_engine.py:267 (sortino = mean/downside_stdev*sqrt(252)), src/modules/backtest/BacktestResultView.tsx:487 (rendered to 2dp beside a correct-looking Sharpe)
notes: Design-it-twice failure (APOSD 10): the block was written once and never checked against a reference. pstdev of the negative subset measures how much the losses differ from EACH OTHER, not their magnitude below zero, so two similar losses drive the denominator toward 0 and the ratio toward infinity. Money-relevant number shown as true and fed to the Critic. One-line fix: downside_dev = math.sqrt(sum(min(r,0.0)**2 for r in returns)/len(returns)), keeping the >0 guard.

refuter.reason: Confirmed: downside deviation is pstdev of the negative-return subset (dispersion among losses, not their magnitude below zero), so the ratio explodes when losses are similar and reads 0.00 when there is <=1 loss or identical losses. Every run with a Sortino is affected.

repro: Run corporate_disclosures._dedup_key over the repo's own two fixtures for the SAME 2026-06-09 RELIANCE announcement (the ICICI Securities investor-meeting update): tests/fixtures/nse/corporate_announcements.json[0] and tests/fixtures/bse/ann_sub_category_get_data.json['Table'][0]. NSE key ('RELIANCE','0136c360465b6a07','2026-06-09') vs BSE key ('RELIANCE','7513e4250c78084a','2026-06-09') -> COLLAPSES: False. The merged feed for any dual-listed name lists every filing twice.
evidence: sidecar/services/corporate_disclosures.py:215, sidecar/services/corporate_disclosures.py:163, sidecar/services/corporate_disclosures.py:251, sidecar/services/corporate_disclosures.py:7, sidecar/services/corporate_disclosures.py:295, sidecar/tests/test_corporate_disclosures.py:141
notes: Obviousness + special-casing to satisfy a test: NSE's headline is attchmntText (the full disclosure body), BSE's is NEWSSUB (the short subject) — different strings, so the SHA-1 of the whole normalized headline can only collapse re-disseminations within one feed. The docstring and the ':295' comment both assert cross-feed dedup works, and test_dedup_collapses_the_same_story_across_exchanges builds a BSE row whose NEWSSUB is literally the NSE row's attchmntText, a shape the live API does not produce. Smallest fix: the BSE row already carries the NSE text in HEADLINE (truncated to 190 chars vs NSE's 326; normalized 120-char prefixes match exactly on the fixtures) — prefer HEADLINE over NEWSSUB at :163 and hash normalized[:120] at :259-260, then re-point the test at the two unmodified fixtures.

refuter.reason: Real: _dedup_key hashes the whole normalized headline, and the NSE lane's headline is attchmntText (full body) while BSE's is NEWSSUB (short subject), so the same filing never collides across feeds; the only cross-feed test overwrites NEWSSUB with the NSE text. title: Nearest-quarter XBRL split merge has no staleness ceiling
repro: A name that stopped filing its SEBI XBRL on BSE years ago but still files the NSE quarterly master: min(with_split, key=lambda p: abs((p.quarter_end - pattern.quarter_end).days)) picks the years-old BSE pattern unconditionally, so the current NSE quarter is enriched with a years-old FII/DII/institutions split.
evidence: sidecar/services/corporate_disclosures.py:530, sidecar/services/corporate_disclosures.py:509
notes: Define errors out of existence: the merge has an 'unavailable' answer already (returning nse_patterns unchanged, :521-523) but no distance bound, so 'nearest' can mean 'three years away'. Compounded by COD-2, which then labels it with the current quarter. Smallest fix: skip the merge when abs((match.quarter_end - pattern.quarter_end).days) exceeds ~200 (two quarters), leaving the split None — the module's own honest default.

refuter.reason: Real, with no distance bound at :530. Live data shows it fires much more than the finding implies, mostly in the other direction: the BSE lane parses a limited set of XBRLs per call (_MAX_SHP_XBRL_PARSES), so OLDER NSE quarters get a FUTURE BSE split copied onto them. SIL's 2021-09-30 through 2024-09-30 quarters all carry the 2024-12-31 split (42.91%, up to 1,188 days away), which fakes a flat FII/DII history. Consumers never read split_as_of.

title: ProviderError->HTTP mapping is duplicated at 25 catch sites in 7 routers beside a global handler; `kind` is honoured in exactly one route, so throttles elsewhere surface as 502
repro: design + code trace: yfinance_provider._provider_error sets kind='rate_limited' for quote/history/fundamentals/income/balance/cashflow/ratings (yfinance_provider.py:53-64, :250, :279, :424-463). Only GET /fundamentals/{symbol} maps it to 429 (+ 'not_found'->404). Every other route — and the app-level handler — emits 502 {detail: str(exc)} and drops kind, so the frontend cannot tell 'throttled, retry later' from 'no data'.
evidence: sidecar/app.py:312-315 (global handler, kind dropped), sidecar/routers/fundamentals.py:104-115 (the one kind-aware site), sidecar/routers/fundamentals.py:219-220,238-239,257-258 (same provider, kind-blind), sidecar/routers/earnings.py:77-78,97-98,116-117,135-136, sidecar/routers/macro.py:55-56,67-68, sidecar/routers/disclosures.py:68-69, sidecar/routers/sec_filings.py:83-84, sidecar/services/errors.py:29-36 (docstring lists only 'rate_limited'|None while 'not_found' is raised at yfinance_provider.py:320,336,341 and provider_registry.py:437)
notes: Repetition (grep 'except ProviderError' sidecar/routers -> 25 hits in earnings, crypto, macro, fundamentals, disclosures, screener, sec_filings) + duplicated truth that has already drifted (1 of 25 sites learned the 429 mapping; `kind: str | None` is an open vocabulary with an undocumented member). R11/D53 introduced kind precisely so a throttle is never reported as absence; at the HTTP boundary that guarantee holds for one endpoint. Smallest fix: make the app-level handler the single mapper ({rate_limited:429, not_found:404, None:502}, optionally echo `kind` in the body), type kind as Literal, and delete the per-route `except ProviderError -> HTTPException(502)` blocks.

refuter.reason: Holds: app-level ProviderError handler emits 502 {detail} and drops kind; 25 'except ProviderError' sites across 7 routers; only GET /fundamentals/{symbol} maps rate_limited->429 and not_found->404; ProviderError docstring documents only 'rate_limited'|None while 'not_found' is raised in yfinance_provider and provider_registry.

title: A BSE 404 is cached as a permanent empty marker, so a bhavcopy requested before publication loses that trading day's close forever
repro: design. _download_bhavcopy writes an empty file to the cache on HTTP 404 ('cache the empty marker') and _bhavcopy_for then reads it and returns None for that day, permanently. Any BSE quote/history call made before BSE publishes the day's bhavcopy (i.e. any intraday request) 404s and poisons that date; after BSE publishes, the cached '' still wins and the day is never re-fetched. The marker has no TTL and nothing invalidates it (data_cache.invalidate is a different store and has no production caller).
evidence: sidecar/services/bse_provider.py:317, sidecar/services/bse_provider.py:287, sidecar/services/bse_provider.py:301
notes: Wrong/stale money data presented as complete. The user sees a BSE chart and quote whose latest bar silently predates the most recent close, for the life of the on-disk cache -- and the correctness gate cannot catch it because the series is internally consistent, just truncated. Smallest fix: never write the empty marker for a day >= today (or stamp the marker with a write time and ignore it when the day is newer than, say, 24 h).

refuter.reason: The poisoning is real, but it runs through a different branch than the one cited. BSE does not 404 an unpublished day: on 2026-09-23 it answered HTTP 200 text/html (14,287 bytes). parse_bhavcopy turns that into an empty frame, and bse_provider.py:329-331 then writes the '' marker, which _bhavcopy_for treats as permanent 'no data' with no TTL. So any BSE history request made on a trading day before publication loses that day's bar for good. The 404 branch at :318 is a second route to the same outcome.

title: A cold-cache BSE range request silently downgrades to <=8 bars, and the series carries no partial-coverage signal
repro: design. _assemble_history walks trading days newest-first with `downloads_left = _MAX_COLD_DOWNLOADS` (8); once spent, every further missing day is skipped. On a cold cache a range='1y' request therefore returns at most 8 daily bars, wrapped in an ordinary OHLCVSeries(symbol, timeframe='1d', bars, provider='bse') -- no coverage field, no partial marker, no warning. The chart renders 8 points as if that were the year.

Smallest fix: add a coverage/partial field to OHLCVSeries (it would also solve the bar_loader reduced-basket problem), or raise when the assembled span covers materially less than the requested range so the registry falls through.

GET /indicators/{sym}?indicators=rsi for the SAME symbol -> EmptySeriesError propagates -> 502. The chart panel shows its honest empty state while the indicator overlay shows a server error.
evidence: sidecar/routers/history.py:71-80 (try/except EmptySeriesError -> 200 empty series with typed reason), sidecar/routers/indicators.py:64 (bare provider_registry.get_history, no handler), sidecar/services/correctness_gate.py:67 (EmptySeriesError exists so '/history' can downgrade)
notes: Consistency violation across sibling routes sharing one provider call; the next maintainer cannot tell which contract is the intended one. Smallest fix: wrap indicators.py:64 in the same except EmptySeriesError and return an IndicatorResponse with empty indicators (the panel already handles an empty overlay), and stamp freshness from the same series.

The chart's indicator effect is not gated on an empty series, so the overlay shows '<msg> (502)' beside the chart's honest empty state; indicators also carry no freshness label.

title: FR-041 provenance/freshness is applied on 2 of 8 data routes; earnings/news/sec return up-to-24h cached payloads with no as-of
repro: GET /earnings/{sym}/history twice within 24h -> the second call is served entirely from data_cache with no field on the wire saying when it was fetched. EarningsHistoryResponse, EarningsSurprisesResponse and EarningsUpcomingResponse carry no as_of/cached_at (only EarningsEstimateDetail has as_of, and it is the PROVIDER's, not the cache's). Same for FilingsListResponse and the news list.
evidence: sidecar/routers/earnings.py:36-38 (_TTL_HISTORY = 24h), sidecar/routers/earnings.py:89-100 (cache read, no stamp), sidecar/models/earnings.py:105-145 (no as_of on 3 of 4 envelopes), sidecar/models/sec.py:143-151, sidecar/models/news.py:15-28; contrast sidecar/models/market.py:26-29 and :50-53 (freshness on Quote and OHLCVSeries)
notes: The product's stated moat is data trust and the FR-041 badge exists to serve it; two routes honour it and six do not, so the badge's absence carries no information. A demanding owner reading a 23-hour-old earnings calendar has no way to know. Smallest fix: have data_cache.get return (value, fetched_at) and stamp a single as_of on each envelope, then reuse the existing StalenessBadge (src/components/DataBadges.tsx:87).

refuter.reason: Earnings envelopes (upcoming/history/surprises) are served from a 6-24h data_cache with no cache as_of — confirmed. Scope corrected: the news half is wrong — news_provider has no cache at all and every NewsItem carries published_at; the SEC list is a 1h cache whose rows each carry filed_date. And what is cached is dated historical events (reported_date, filed_date), not a value claiming to be current, so the gap hides a <=24h cache lag (e.g. a just-reported quarter missing on earnings day), not a stale price shown as live — low.

title: News symbol tagging false-positives on single-letter tickers (A matches the English article)
repro: Verified by running the router's matcher verbatim: tag('Nvidia unveils a new chip','A report from a bank',['A']) -> ['A'] ; tag('Fed holds rates','The T-bill curve steepened',['T','F','C']) -> ['T']. So GET /news?symbols=A (Agilent) returns essentially the entire feed tagged as Agilent news; T (AT&T), F (Ford), C (Citi), K, M, V, X, Z behave the same.
evidence: sidecar/routers/news.py:69-74 (case-insensitive \b{symbol}\b over title+summary), sidecar/routers/news.py:62-68 (docstring claims the word-boundary anchor prevents exactly this)
notes: The docstring's example is 'A does not match every word starting with a' -- true, and it misses the real failure, which is the standalone article 'a'/'A'. Consequence: every headline is attributed to the ticker, sentiment for that symbol becomes market-wide noise, and the agent reading /news inherits the mis-attribution. Same function as -3, opposite failure direction, one fix covers both. Smallest fix: require len(symbol) >= 2 for bare-text matching and fall back to the resolved company name for 1-character tickers (the alias set from -3 supplies it).

refuter.reason: Reproduced by running routers.news._tag_symbols in the sidecar venv: case-insensitive \bA\b matches the article 'A'/'a', and \bT\b matches 'T-bill'. A watchlist holding A/T/F/C/etc. gets general headlines attributed and kept as that ticker's news. Same function as -3, opposite failure direction.

title: Analyst + earnings per-symbol caches are permanent for the session: no TTL, no invalidation, no refresh path, no as-of shown
repro: Open Analyst Ratings, load AAPL (succeeds). Any later change upstream is invisible: pressing Load with 'AAPL' again sets the same string so React bails and the effect never re-runs; the Retry button calls the same cached accessor, which short-circuits on the cache. No control in the panel can re-fetch, and no timestamp is rendered. Same for the earnings drill-down caches (history/surprises/estimates).
evidence: src/store/analyst-ratings.ts:51-54, src/store/analyst-ratings.ts:79-82, src/store/analyst-ratings.ts:107-110, src/store/earnings.ts:105-108, src/store/earnings.ts:133-136, src/store/earnings.ts:161-164, src/modules/analyst-ratings/AnalystRatingsPanel.tsx:71-77, src/modules/analyst-ratings/AnalystRatingsPanel.tsx:96-102, src/modules/equity-overview/EquityOverviewPanel.tsx:286-314, src/store/sec.ts:82
notes: Define-errors-out-of-existence + consistency: `const cached = get().histories[normalized]; if (cached) return cached;` has no timestamp, so staleness is structurally indistinguishable from freshness. Consequence: analyst ratings / price targets / earnings surprises loaded at 09:00 are still shown after an 11:00 downgrade, with nothing on screen saying when they were fetched — on the axis the product calls its moat (data trust). The sibling EquityOverviewPanel DOES badge provider + freshness/as-of (ProvenanceBadge), so the gap is inconsistent inside one subsystem. Secondary: every cache is an unbounded Record with no eviction; store/sec.ts:82 filingDetailByAccession holds whole parsed filings. Smallest fix: store {payload, fetchedAt}, treat older-than-N-minutes as a miss, render fetchedAt as an as-of chip, and give each panel a Refresh that bypasses the cache — the in-repo precedent is NewsFeedPanel.tsx:209-257 (refreshNonce).

refuter.reason: Real: every getX in both stores returns the cached payload unconditionally, with no timestamp and no eviction. The Load button sets the same symbol string and retryTab calls the same short-circuiting accessor, so nothing in the panel can refetch, and no as-of is shown. The headline mechanism is overstated, though: the sidecar route caches the same data for 6 h (ratings) or 24 h (earnings history), so a frontend refresh would not reveal an 11:00 downgrade after a 09:00 load anyway. The frontend's permanence only adds staleness beyond the sidecar TTL in long desktop sessions. The durable defect is the missing as-of and the missing refresh on a data-trust surface: medium, not high.

evidence: sidecar/services/openbb_mcp_provider.py:244, sidecar/services/openbb_mcp_provider.py:249, sidecar/services/openbb_mcp_provider.py:250, sidecar/services/openbb_mcp_provider.py:187, sidecar/services/sec_filings_provider.py:158, sidecar/routers/mcp.py:44
notes: Obviousness: the try/except at :243-248 wraps ONLY client.call_tool; _decode_tool_result at :249 raises ProviderError on isError, on non-JSON text and on 'no text content', and every one of those paths exits before the `_last_tool_call_ok = True` at :250 AND before any `= False` - leaving the previous value in place. title: Sidecar position PUT/DELETE sync is dead by construction — the SQLite ledger never sees an update or a delete
repro: Agent applies portfolio_update_position or portfolio_delete_position with the position_id it read from get_portfolio (a frontend holding id, e.g. "h-3f2a..."): sidecarPositionId does Number("h-3f2a...") -> NaN -> returns undefined -> portfolioUrl(undefined) -> PUT/DELETE http://127.0.0.1:<port>/portfolio/positions -> FastAPI declares those methods only at /positions/{position_id} -> 405 -> syncPositionToSidecar returns false -> the boolean is discarded. The row stays in portfolio.db unchanged forever.
evidence: src/lib/host-actions.ts:1313-1317 (sidecarPositionId), 1255-1259 (portfolioUrl), 1306 (return response.ok || 404), 1361 and 1381 (return value discarded); sidecar/services/agent_tools/catalog.py:1345 ("position_id": {"type": "string"}); src/lib/host-actions.ts:550 (resolveHolding matches the frontend holding id); sidecar/routers/portfolio.py:33,42 (PUT/DELETE only at /positions/{position_id}); sidecar/routers/portfolio.py:21,27 (GET/POST at /positions)
notes: Define-errors-out-of-existence violated: the failure was made unrepresentable by discarding it, not by preventing it. The SQLite table is append-only by accident — POST lands, PUT/DELETE never do — so it diverges monotonically from the store. Latent today because nothing reads it (see COD-portfolio-3); it becomes wrong money the moment any feature does. Smallest fix: delete the sync with the rest of the ledger (COD-portfolio-3). If the ledger must stay: read the sidecar's assigned integer id from the POST response (host-actions.ts:1337 currently discards it) and persist it on the Holding so PUT/DELETE address a real row.

refuter.reason: The mechanism is real. Holding ids are 'h-<uuid>' (portfolios.ts genId), so sidecarPositionId returns undefined and PUT/DELETE go to the bare /portfolio/positions, which has no PUT/DELETE route (only GET/POST); syncPositionToSidecar's return value is then discarded. Corrected from high to medium: no product surface reads the ledger (see COD-portfolio-3), so no user flow breaks or degrades today; the harm is a diverging dead table that would mislead a future maintainer.

title: Holding validation lives in the panel form, not in the store — the workspace-restore path accepts negative quantity/cost and coerces garbage to 0
repro: A workspace blob (or any non-form caller) carrying {symbol:"RELIANCE", quantity:"abc", costBasis:-100} restores through setAll -> normalizeHolding -> quantity 0, costBasis -100 accepted. The holding counts in positionCount, publishes to the agent with marketValue 0, and shows a negative cost in the table. The form path would have rejected both ("Quantity must be greater than 0", "Cost basis cannot be negative").
evidence: src/store/portfolios.ts:69-89 (normalizeHolding: no sign checks; 84-85 coerce non-finite to 0), 186-206 (setAll — the workspace-restore path — runs the same normalizer); contrast src/modules/portfolio/PortfolioPanel.tsx:266-277 (form guards) and src/lib/host-actions.ts:1334,1358 (agent guards quantity > 0); the validating model sidecar/models/portfolio.py:36-39 (gt=0, ge=0) sits on the dead path (COD-portfolio-3)

Smallest fix: in normalizeHolding, return null when quantity is not finite or <= 0, or when costBasis is not finite or < 0 — one place, inherited by the form, the agent path and workspace restore.

It is also broader than stated: the agent apply path at host-actions.ts:1334/1358 guards only quantity > 0, and the catalog schema puts no minimum on cost_basis, so a negative agent-supplied cost basis also lands in the store.

title: SSRF guard validates the input URL but the transport follows redirects, so a research visit can fetch loopback/link-local/LAN targets
repro: A search result URL on a public host answers 302 -> http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/ (or http://127.0.0.1:<sidecar port>/agents, or a LAN host). fetch_page calls is_public_http_url ONCE on the input URL (extract.py:593), which passes; httpx_fetch opens its client with follow_redirects=True (transport.py:108); the redirected body is main-content-extracted and returned as `content`, then wrapped into the synthesis prompt and the published brief. The post-redirect URL is available as fetched.url and is stored as `final_url` (extract.py:635) but never re-validated. Same hole on the PDF lane: extract.py:307 follow_redirects=True and the curl_cffi lane at extract.py:293-294 (follows redirects by default).
evidence: sidecar/services/search/extract.py:593, sidecar/services/search/extract.py:635, sidecar/services/search/extract.py:307, sidecar/services/search/extract.py:293, sidecar/services/search/transport.py:108, sidecar/services/search/extract.py:12
notes: Violates information hiding: the security decision leaks out of the guard because the guard sits at the call site instead of below the fetch. The module docstring (extract.py:12-14) explicitly promises 'a research visit must never become a port-scan of localhost' - the invariant is asserted in prose and not held by the structure. Attacker controls the redirect target AFTER the check has passed, so every knob is on their side; there is also a plain DNS-rebinding TOCTOU (is_public_http_url resolves, then httpx resolves again). Consequence: arbitrary internal HTTP GET with the response body exfiltrated into a user-visible brief. Smallest fix: set follow_redirects=False in httpx_fetch and walk redirects through is_public_http_url inside the transport (or attach an httpx event hook that rejects a non-public response.url), so fetch_page, _default_pdf_fetch, the impersonation lane and every future lane inherit the guard.

refuter.reason: The bypass is real and I reproduced it live. fetch_page checks is_public_http_url once, on the input URL only (extract.py:593). httpx_fetch then follows redirects (transport.py:108), the PDF lane does too (extract.py:307), and nothing re-checks fetched.url. Two corrections: the sidecar's own loopback JSON endpoints (the raw finding's /agents example) are rejected by the content-type filter at extract.py:620-621, so only HTML/text/PDF internal targets reach `content`. And the extracted text goes to the user's own brief and their BYOK model, not back to the attacker. That makes this a real guard bypass with no demonstrated exfiltration channel, so high rather than critical.

title: The live-lookup LRU has no TTL, so a successful empty result is cached for the sidecar's lifetime
repro: First resolve of an unknown name falls to _live_lookup, which caches the result -- INCLUDING a successful empty search -- under (query, region) with no expiry (only a 128-entry LRU bound). A symbol listed after that first miss stays unresolvable for that query string until the desktop app restarts.
evidence: sidecar/services/symbol_resolver.py:124, sidecar/services/symbol_resolver.py:990, sidecar/services/symbol_resolver.py:1033, sidecar/services/symbol_resolver.py:982
notes: Design for the future: the docstring states caching the empty result is deliberate (avoid re-hitting the network) and the 60 s failure cooldown is the right shape -- but a NEGATIVE result is the one kind that goes stale, and the terminal is a long-lived desktop process, not a request-scoped server. Memory is bounded; freshness is not. Smallest fix: store (timestamp, rows) and treat an entry older than a few minutes as a miss -- or cache only non-empty results, letting the existing cooldown absorb the repeat-miss traffic.

refuter.reason: Holds: _live_lookup caches the result, including an empty successful search, under (query, region) with only a 128-entry LRU bound and no timestamp, so a negative result persists for the sidecar's lifetime. Because the masters are bundled snapshots, the live rung is the ONLY path to a post-snapshot listing, which makes a stale negative a real miss.

title: Resolver has no former-name data; searching the bank's documented pre-2010 legal name ranks a dead ghost instrument above the real bank
repro: GET http://127.0.0.1:52152/resolve?q=Dhanalakshmi+Bank (fresh fetch, 2026-09-23, isolated sidecar) -> needs_disambiguation: true, candidates[0] = {symbol: 'DHAN-RE', name: 'Dhanlaxmi Bank Ltd', exchange: 'BSE', confidence: 0.7429, bse_code: '750942'} ranked ABOVE candidates[1] = {symbol: 'DHANBANK', confidence: 0.6667, bse_code: '532180'}, the actual listed, trading bank. DHAN-RE is the January-2025 Rights Entitlement (ISIN INE680A20011) -- an expired, non-trading line with no price, exactly the 'ghost instrument' the pack flags as a trap. Every candidate in every resolve response for this entity (resolve_bare_symbol, resolve_company_name, resolve_bse_code, and this fresh former-name query) carries former_name: null, confirming the resolver never populated the field despite the bank's well-documented 2010-08-10 rename from 'Dhanalakshmi Bank' to 'Dhanlaxmi Bank' (and a third spelling, 'Dhanalaxmi', in the issuer's own current annual-report filename).
evidence: collected 'resolve_company_name' call in docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/collected/P12_DHANBANK.json (former_name: null on every candidate); fresh GET /resolve?q=Dhanalakshmi+Bank on 2026-09-23 against http://127.0.0.1:52152 (candidates[0].symbol='DHAN-RE' confidence 0.7429 > candidates[1].symbol='DHANBANK' confidence 0.6667, former_name null on both)
notes: Principle violated: a symbol resolver that ranks fuzzy-name matches needs the entity's alias history to rank correctly, and this is a live, reproducible failure mode, not a hypothetical -- a user typing the bank's own former legal name is handed a dead rights-entitlement instrument as the TOP candidate. Smallest fix shape: populate former_name (and the 'Dhanalaxmi' filename-spelling alias) in the resolver's name index for this entity, and/or down-weight or exclude expired/delisted rights-entitlement lines (asset class or a 'delisted'/'expired' flag) from fuzzy company-name ranking generally.

refuter.reason: The ranking defect reproduces, but the mechanism is misattributed: Instrument.former_name is by design the retired NSE SYMBOL from the rename lane (symbol_resolver.py:239, 896), not a company-name alias, and DHANBANK's ticker never changed, so null there is correct. The real cause is that the bundled BSE master's expired rights-entitlement line DHAN-RE (ISIN INE680A20011, asset_class 'equity') is never filtered from fuzzy name ranking -- it outranks the bank for 'Dhanalakshmi Bank' (0.7429 vs 0.6667) and TIES it at 1.0 for the exact current name 'Dhanlaxmi Bank', forcing disambiguation on the bank's own name. Severity lowered to medium: the real bank is always in the candidate list and disambiguation is explicit (not a silent wrong resolve), though picking the top row lands on a dead instrument.

title: revenue_ttm and net_income_ttm fabricate a TTM figure by synthesizing a phantom quarter for a company that has no true TTM
repro: GET http://127.0.0.1:52152/fundamentals/JONJUA -> revenue_ttm: 239033504.0 (INR 23.9034 crore), net_income_ttm: 87482000.0 (INR 8.7482 crore), growth_basis: 'mrq_yoy'. Outside truth (screener.in, the only figure obtainable, since JONJUA has NO true trailing-twelve-months data -- it reported HALF-YEARLY until FY26 and only 3 discrete quarters have ever been filed: Dec-2025 sales 1.54cr/np 1.23cr, Mar-2026 sales 16.36cr/np 5.72cr, Jun-2026 sales 4.35cr/np 1.24cr) gives FY2025-26 full-year standalone revenue 21.21cr and net profit 8.07cr -- 12.7% and 8.4% BELOW the app's TTM figures respectively. Reconstructing the app's arithmetic: summing the 3 known filed quarters (1.54+16.36+4.35=22.25cr revenue, 1.23+5.72+1.24=8.19cr profit) plus HALF of the H1-FY26 half-year figure (FY26 total 21.21cr minus the two known H2 quarters 17.90cr = 3.31cr H1; half = 1.655cr revenue, and correspondingly ~0.56cr profit) reproduces the app's revenue_ttm (22.25+1.655=23.905, vs app's 23.9034) and net_income_ttm (8.19+0.56=8.75, vs app's 8.7482) almost exactly -- yfinance is treating half of a NEVER-FILED-AS-A-QUARTER half-year figure as if it were a discrete quarter to fill the fourth TTM slot.

Any product that prints TTM for this name is asserting a number nobody has filed.')
notes: Principle violated: the pack explicitly names this exact failure mode as the highest-value trap in the collection, and the app falls into it precisely -- presenting a specific, decimal-precise 'TTM' revenue and profit figure for a company whose own reporting history makes a genuine TTM impossible to construct, built by silently averaging in a half-filed period as if it were a real quarter. Concrete consequence: a user comparing JONJUA's 'TTM' P/E, growth or profitability against peers is comparing against a number nobody at the company has ever filed or audited. Smallest fix shape: when a company's income-statement periods are annual-only or show reporting-cadence gaps (an explicit yfinance quarterly-financials call returning fewer than 4 well-formed quarters), suppress or clearly re-label the *_ttm fields as 'FY<year> annual' rather than presenting yfinance's own synthetic TTM as fact.

But the value is not shown to be wrong: the FY26 annual (21.21 cr / 8.07 cr) is a different period, so the '12.7% below' comparison is as-of/definitional skew by the diff stage's own rules. The true Jul-25..Jun-26 revenue must lie in [22.25, 25.56] cr (3 filed quarters + 0..3.31 cr of H1), and the app's 23.90 cr is inside that range. title: Quote, fundamentals and every valuation ratio for NuScale Power Corp (NYSE:SMR) silently serve the real numbers of an unrelated BSE SME jewellery company that happens to share the ticker 'SMR'
repro: GET http://127.0.0.1:52152/quotes/SMR?asset_class=equity (or /fundamentals/SMR) while the session's active region is IN (config.get_region()). Response is a real, well-formed 200: price 95.0 INR / BSE / 2026-09-18 (collected.json:175-195), fundamentals.name 'SMR Jewels Limited', sector 'Consumer Cyclical', industry 'Luxury Goods', pe_ratio 17.03, roe 66.65%, debt_to_equity 0.345, revenue_ttm INR 4.32B, net_income_ttm INR 247M positive, eps 5.58, fifty_two_week_high/low 115.0/75.85 INR (collected.json:196-322). Every one of these is SMR Jewels Ltd's (BSE 544774) real data, not NuScale's. The true target (per this pack, sourced from SEC EDGAR/XBRL) is: last close $8.27 USD, sector 'Boiler Shops'/'Industrials'/'electricity-energy-uranium' (three conflicting but genuine classifications, none of them 'Luxury Goods'), pe_ttm 'loss-making' (PE n/a), roe -55.18%, debt_to_equity ~0.0 (effectively debt-free), revenue_ttm $10.69M, net_profit_ttm -$415.7M to -$672.9M (never profitable since the 2022 business combination), eps_ttm -$1.54 to -$2.92, week52 range $7.21-$57.42. The /resolve?q=SMR call itself shows both candidates at confidence 1.0 (collected.json:33-60) -- BSE 'SMR Jewels Ltd' and US 'NUSCALE POWER Corp' -- and binds to the BSE one because the session's default region is IN; every downstream money-data route then re-queries the bare symbol with no way to carry the correct region forward.
evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/collected/P20_SMR.json:11-66 (resolve, region IN, binds to BSE Jewels despite a tied US candidate), :175-503 (quote + fundamentals block, all SMR Jewels data), :2300-2321 (ratings, also SMR Jewels-scoped, symbol 'SMR.BO'); docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/packs/P20_SMR.json (outside truth, NuScale, every field sourced to SEC EDGAR/XBRL or a corroborating aggregator) and its P20-T1 trap note; sidecar/routers/quotes.py:52-53 (get_quote(symbol, asset_class) -- no region parameter of any kind); sidecar/routers/fundamentals.py:88-89,102-103 (get_fundamentals(symbol) -- same), :177-180 (income), :183-186 (balance), :189-192 (cashflow), :195-198 (ratings) -- none of the five symbol-scoped fundamentals routes accept a region override, in contrast to :147-174 in the SAME file where get_company_narrative DOES thread an X-Vysted-Region header through to the service layer; sidecar/services/provider_registry.py:448,455 (get_quote already accepts an optional region kwarg the router never passes), :473,483-492 (get_fundamentals, same), :288-302 (_effective_region: 'an ambiguous bare ticker defers to the user's locale' -- by design, but nothing above this layer ever supplies the disambiguating region for these five routes); sidecar/services/resolution_policy.py:81-96 (_residual_tie's own docstring: 'A cross-region tie is NOT residual: region is the separating evidence... so the bind stands' -- confirms /resolve's bind-without-disambiguating is intentional design, which makes the missing region propagation on the data routes the actual gap, not a resolver bug).
notes: Root cause: sidecar/services/provider_registry.py's get_quote/get_fundamentals/get_income_statement/get_balance_sheet/get_cash_flow/get_analyst_rating all already accept an optional `region` parameter specifically to route between the US (yfinance) and IN (nse/bse) providers, and resolution_policy.py already treats region as the correct disambiguator for a cross-region ticker collision (by explicit design, per its own docstring) -- but the FastAPI routes in routers/quotes.py and routers/fundamentals.py never expose that parameter to a caller, so the region propagation the design assumes stops at /resolve and never reaches the routes that actually serve the numbers. For a genuinely colliding ticker like SMR (NYSE + an unrelated BSE SME), this means there is no way, even in principle, for a caller who has correctly resolved the intended instrument (e.g. via /resolve?q=NuScale+Power+Corp, which DOES correctly return region US, confidence 1.0 -- see the diff file's supplementary entry) to then fetch that instrument's quote or fundamentals: every subsequent call is keyed by the bare symbol alone and silently re-resolves to whichever region the session defaults to. The harm is squarely 'wrong money-relevant data shown as true' with no error, no warning, and no identity_note (fundamentals.identity_note is null in the collected response) -- exactly the class of bug the product's stated 'data trust' moat exists to prevent, and it hits the exact collision battery slot P20 was built to probe. Contrast: the one part of this collection that IS correct for NuScale is /fundamentals/SMR/income|balance|cashflow (see the diff file's income_statement match entry) -- but only because that trio is served by a different provider (openbb-mcp) whose own bare-symbol default happens to favour the US listing here; the identical mechanism is what makes DAT-P9-1 (battery slot P9/P19, ticker AMAL) wrong in the opposite direction, so this is a systemic provider-default hazard, not something specific to SMR that happens to work out. Smallest fix shape: add `region: str | None = Query(None)` (matching routers/resolve.py's own existing pattern) to get_quote/get_quotes in quotes.py and to get_fundamentals/get_income_statement/get_balance_sheet/get_cash_flow/get_analyst_rating in fundamentals.py, threading it into the already-region-aware provider_registry calls exactly as get_company_narrative already does for X-Vysted-Region three routes below it in the same file -- then have the frontend pass the region from whichever /resolve candidate the user actually picked, so a disambiguated instrument stays disambiguated all the way to the panel that renders its numbers.

refuter.reason: The defect is real, and it is worse than filed. In an IN session the equity-overview fan-out for SMR serves SMR Jewels' quote, fundamentals and ratings (SMR.BO) but NuScale's income statement (USD revenue 31.48M FY2025), so one panel shows two companies' numbers with identity_note null. The mechanism is corrected: the sidecar is not region-blind. _RegionMiddleware applies X-Vysted-Region to every route, and with `X-Vysted-Region: US` the same /quotes/SMR and /fundamentals/SMR return NuScale correctly (USD 8.89, ROE -55.18%, 52w 7.21-57.42, which matches the pack). The gap is in the frontend: sidecar-client sends the session-wide settings region on every call, and loadEquityOverview fans out on the bare symbol, dropping the region of the /resolve candidate the user picked. The smallest fix is to pass the picked candidate's region as a per-call header override (sidecarGet already lets per-call headers win) or to key calls by yahoo_symbol, and to make the income/balance/cashflow leg respect that region.

evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/collected/P6_ICON.json:547-2007 (income/balance/cashflow bodies, provider 'openbb-mcp'); cross-checked against docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/packs/P6_ICON.json:'latest_results'/'traps.eps_series_not_restated_1000x' (Icon Facilitators' real net profit series 0.94/1.92/1.76/4.47/4.42 INR crore, all positive, March fiscal year)
notes: Mechanism: pack's own traps.three_way_in_app_ticker_collision (packs/P6_ICON.json:'traps'[0]) documents that the app's own us_instruments.json master resolves the bare string 'ICON' to a second, unrelated company ('Icon Energy Corp', US). The /fundamentals/ICON top-level summary (yfinance-sourced, collected.json:239-546) IS correctly scoped to the Indian entity -- market cap, shares outstanding (7,859,600), revenue_ttm and book_value all reconcile to Icon Facilitators' real figures -- so the resolver itself is not misfiring for that call. But the three openbb-mcp-backed statement sub-routes return numbers with the shape of a different, tiny, loss-making, Dec-FY company. Consequence: any panel or agent tool that renders 'Financials' (income statement / balance sheet / cash flow history) for this BSE SME stock would show a stranger's numbers as this company's numbers -- exactly the class of wrong-money-data-shown-as-true defect the R15 brief flags as the top data-trust risk. Smallest fix shape: audit the /fundamentals/{symbol}/income|balance|cashflow route's symbol resolution for the openbb-mcp provider specifically (it appears to key off something other than the ISIN/BSE-code-scoped resolution used by the top-level /fundamentals and /disclosures routes) and add a same-entity sanity check (e.g. shares_outstanding order-of-magnitude match, fiscal-year-end match) before serving statement data for an ambiguous ticker.

refuter.reason: Holds exactly. The statement routes pass the bare user string to openbb-mcp, whose _normalize_symbol only swaps dots for dashes and forwards 'ICON' to its yfinance backend, which answers with the US-listed Icon Energy Corp (Greece, USD). No correctness validator runs on statements (validate=None), unlike /fundamentals. The live stack still serves Icon Energy's Dec-FY net income (-4,197,000 / -210,000 / 1,155,000 / 4,242,000), which matches yfinance's 'ICON' ticker number for number, as financials for Icon Facilitators (BSE 544426). One refinement: nothing is misresolved in the first place. The bare ticker is never resolved to the BSE listing at all (yfinance_provider._yahoo_symbol, which maps BSE-only names to .BO, is only the rank-2 fallback and is never reached).

title: Results-calendar endpoint fails outright for a BSE-only SME stock with a misleading NSE-specific error, even though real half-yearly results exist
repro: GET http://127.0.0.1:52152/disclosures/results?symbol=ICON -> HTTP 502, body {"detail": "nse_direct: 'ICON' is not a known NSE instrument"}. Icon Facilitators is legitimately BSE-listed (bse_code 544426) with no NSE listing at all (confirmed on both sides) and has four genuine half-yearly result periods on record (Sep 2024 through Mar 2026) per screener.
evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/collected/P6_ICON.json:2155-2166; docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/packs/P6_ICON.json:'latest_results' (full H2 FY26 figures: sales 34.45cr, net profit 2.89cr, eps 3.68, opm 12.02%, plus 3 prior half-years, all screener-sourced)
notes: Mechanism: the results/earnings-calendar route appears to be hardcoded to (or defaults to) an NSE-only data path, and fails hard for a stock that was never expected to have an NSE listing rather than falling back to BSE. Consequence: the app cannot surface ANY results data for this route on a real, actively-reporting, BSE-only SME name, and the error text actively misattributes the cause ('not a known NSE instrument') rather than saying 'BSE-only, no results-calendar coverage.' A user or agent tool calling this route for any BSE-SME name would hit the same wall. Smallest fix shape: route /disclosures/results by exchange (use the resolver's exchange field) and either serve a BSE-sourced results path or return an honest 'not available for BSE-only listings yet' rather than a wrong-exchange error.

refuter.reason: Real, but the finding overstates it. The results-calendar service is NSE-only by construction: nse_provider.get_results_calendar has no BSE lane, unlike get_shareholding, which has NSE+BSE lanes. So every BSE-only name gets a 502 with the misleading 'not a known NSE instrument' text, and the live stack reproduces this. Two corrections take it from high to medium. First, the route serves board-meeting and results DATES (purpose/date events), not results figures, so 'cannot surface ANY results data' is wrong. The half-year figures the finding cites as outside truth are a different field, and the pack records the filing dates themselves as a world gap. Second, the failure is loud, not silent. Its only other consumer, research/disclosures.fetch_results_calendar, degrades softly to ok:false.

evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/collected/P6_ICON.json:239-538 (full fundamentals body -- no roce field present); docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/packs/P6_ICON.json:'roce'

ROCE is a headline ratio on screener.in, the product's stated data benchmark, and a core screen for Indian small-cap investors. This is a real completeness gap at medium. title: Day volume is null in the quote for ICON despite the quote otherwise being fully populated for the same session
repro: GET http://127.0.0.1:52152/quotes/ICON?asset_class=equity -> volume: null, while price/change/change_percent/timestamp for the same 2026-09-18 session are all correctly populated. Outside truth: 9,600 shares, corroborated by screener, Groww AND INDmoney all independently.
evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/collected/P6_ICON.json:218-238 (quote body, volume: null on line 227); docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/packs/P6_ICON.json:'price.volume'
notes: A silent blank on a field the world has (and triple-corroborates) for the exact same session the app otherwise renders correctly. On a name this illiquid (9,600 shares / ~INR 6.2 lakh traded), volume is one of the few real signals available (per the pack's own 'illiquidity' trap, a missing volume also makes any liquidity/technical-indicator gating impossible to apply correctly). Smallest fix shape: check why the BSE quote provider path that supplies price/change is not also supplying the same day's traded volume that these third-party aggregators clearly have.

refuter.reason: Holds, and it is structural rather than ICON-specific. bse_provider._quote_from_header reads h.get('Volume') or h.get('TotalTradedQty'), but BSE's getScripHeaderData payload carries neither key: the Header object has PrevClose/Open/High/Low/LTP/Ason and no volume at all. So EVERY header-path BSE quote ships volume=null, even though the bhavcopy fallback (_quote_from_bhavcopy) carries real volume. Side observation for the lead: the live quote is stamped timestamp 2026-09-23 via most_recent_session, while BSE's own 'Ason' says 22 Sep 26 16:00, so the session label also ignores the header's as-of.

title: Trailing-12m dividend per share is null instead of a confirmed true zero
repro: GET http://127.0.0.1:52152/fundamentals/ICON -> dividend_per_share_ttm: null, field_meta reason 'provider did not publish this field'. Outside truth: screener's own annual P&L shows Dividend Payout % = 0.00% in every year FY22 through FY26 -- a confirmed, sourced, real zero, not an unknown.
evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/collected/P6_ICON.json:281 (dividend_per_share_ttm), :377-383 (field_meta 'unavailable'); docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/packs/P6_ICON.json:'dividend.paid_trailing_12m_per_share'
notes: The app conflates 'we don't know' with 'this company pays zero dividends,' the same missing-value-rendered-as-zero-or-vice-versa class of trap the pack's own collector flags elsewhere for a third-party aggregator (INDmoney's P/E-shown-as-0 trap) -- except here it runs the opposite direction (a real, confirmed zero is shown as unknown). A user relying on this field for a 'no dividend' screen would see a blank instead of the confirmed answer. Smallest fix shape: when the underlying provider has no dividend history at all for a name, and the company's own filed payout ratio is 0% across all available years, surface 0 rather than null (or at minimum distinguish 'confirmed zero' from 'provider gap' in field_meta, the way the app already does for other fields).

refuter.reason: The gap is real but the mechanism is misdescribed and the severity overstated. dividend_per_share_ttm is a DERIVED field that /fundamentals never computes: it is excluded from field_meta stamping, and the cited 'provider did not publish' meta at collected:377-383 belongs to dividend_per_share, not _ttm. The research FAST leg fills it via dividend_history, which deliberately returns 'unavailable' for an EMPTY dividend series, because never-paid and data-missing cannot be told apart from that alone. So a lifetime non-payer like ICON is shown as honestly-labelled unknown, never as the confirmed 0. That is a conservative design choice with a reason attached, not a silent blank, so the severity goes to low. The fix is to affirm zero when price history covers 12 months or more and the dividend series is empty.

title: Announcements feed returns zero results for JUMBO despite real, recent, material BSE filings

evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/collected/P7_JUMBO.json:3958-3971 (empty announcements body); cross-checked against docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/packs/P7_JUMBO.json:'last_3_announcements' (3 real BSE filings between 2026-07-30 and 2026-07-31, incl. https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=64e3126e-2c55-47d5-8201-dd24c2391b80.pdf, the 36th AGM outcome PDF that was opened and read directly, confirming a dividend-declaration resolution)
notes: Mechanism: the route reports success (status 200, errors:{}) with a genuinely empty result set for a BSE-only nano-cap that has filed a dividend-declaring AGM outcome, a director appointment and a scrutiniser's e-voting report within the prior two months. Consequence: a user or agent checking 'what's new' for this stock sees a clean empty state that reads as 'no recent activity' when in fact a dividend was just declared -- silently misleading, worse than an explicit error because there is no signal anything failed. Smallest fix shape: since 'sources': ['BSE'] is reported but produced nothing, audit the BSE announcements fetch path for a BSE-only scrip code (516078) -- likely the same NSE-first assumption implicated in DAT-P7-2's 502 (results calendar), applied here to the announcements source selection/parsing.

refuter.reason: The empty feed is real but the stated mechanism is wrong: the BSE lane ran and succeeded (sources:['BSE'], errors:{}); it returns nothing because _fetch_bse_announcements hard-codes a 30-day date window (_BSE_ANN_WINDOW_DAYS=30), and BSE's own feed shows JUMBO's newest filing is 2026-07-31, i.e. 50 days before the 2026-09-19 collection, so nothing falls inside the window. It is not an NSE-first assumption. Severity stays high because research relies on this feed to reach 'a quarter-old results filing' through limit=50 (research/disclosures.py:34-38). The date window defeats that silently for any infrequent BSE filer: the agent tool returns ok:True with an empty list, and the response never states the window. Correction on the framing: BSE's CorporateAction record shows no 2026 dividend, so 'a dividend was just declared' is not supported by the exchange record. Fix: page by count, not a 30-day window, or widen the window and return it in the response.

title: Results/filing-calendar route hard-fails (502) for a BSE-only stock instead of degrading gracefully
repro: GET http://127.0.0.1:52152/disclosures/results?symbol=JUMBO -> HTTP 502 {"detail": "nse_direct: 'JUMBO' is not a known NSE instrument"}
evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/collected/P7_JUMBO.json:3974-3985; docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/packs/P7_JUMBO.json:'latest_results' (Q1 FY2026-27, filed 2026-07-30, sourced from screener.in's scraped BSE announcement list) and 'traps'[1] ("BSE-ONLY listing, no NSE symbol at all. A pipeline that defaults to an NSE-first data source... will find nothing for this name")
notes: Mechanism: the results-calendar route is hardwired to an NSE-only provider ('nse_direct') with no BSE fallback, so it throws a raw upstream error string straight through as a 502 for any BSE-only listing -- exactly the trap the pack's own traps section flags as a class-level pipeline hazard, now confirmed as a live bug rather than a hypothetical risk. Consequence: any panel/agent surfacing 'latest results' or a results calendar for a BSE-only name (a large share of Indian small/nano-caps) gets a hard error instead of the BSE-sourced results date the outside world has. Smallest fix shape: gate the nse_direct call on exchange presence (skip/fall back to a BSE results-date source when resolve.exchange == 'BSE' and no NSE symbol exists) instead of letting the NSE provider's own not-found error propagate as a 502.

refuter.reason: Confirmed: get_results_calendar calls only nse_provider, with no exchange gate and no BSE fallback, and the router turns the ProviderError into a 502 that carries the raw 'nse_direct: ... not a known NSE instrument' string. Severity corrected from high to medium because no frontend code calls /disclosures/results (grep of src/ finds nothing), and the one in-product consumer, research's fetch_results_calendar, degrades honestly to {ok:False, error:'results calendar unavailable: ...'}. What remains is a real gap: a BSE-only listing has no results-calendar source at all, and a raw 502 comes back where a 200 with an empty list or an 'NSE-only feed' note would fit.

title: Derived per-share ratios (EPS, book value per share) contradict the app's own freshly-fetched income/balance-sheet data for the same symbol
repro: GET http://127.0.0.1:52152/fundamentals/JUMBO -> eps=13.69, book_value=54.361. In the SAME collection run, GET .../fundamentals/JUMBO/balance -> Stockholders Equity FY2026=477,377,000; and .../fundamentals/JUMBO net_income_ttm=116,379,000, shares_outstanding=8,373,700 -> 116379000/8373700=13.90 and 477377000/8373700=57.01, neither of which matches the reported eps/book_value fields.
evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/collected/P7_JUMBO.json:243 (book_value=54.361), :246 (eps=13.69), :259-262 (revenue_ttm/net_income_ttm/shares_outstanding), :1211-1219 (Stockholders Equity, balance sheet); outside cross-check docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/packs/P7_JUMBO.json:eps_ttm (13.89, sum of last 4 quarterly EPS, confirmed independently by BSE ComHeadernew EPS=13.90) and book_value_per_share (57.0, screener.in)
notes: Mechanism: the app's own raw ingredients for both ratios (net_income_ttm/shares_outstanding for EPS; stockholders_equity/shares_outstanding for book value) compute to values that match outside truth almost exactly (13.90 and 57.01), yet the 'eps' and 'book_value' fields in the SAME payload report 13.69 (-1.4%) and 54.361 (-4.9%) respectively. This is not a provider-basis disagreement like pe_ttm/pb/roe (where two outside sources also disagree with each other) -- here the app contradicts ITSELF, strongly suggesting these two ratio fields are sourced from a stale/differently-scoped yfinance 'info' snapshot rather than computed from the same financial-statement data the app already fetches and serves elsewhere in the response. Consequence: a user trusting the headline eps/book_value fields sees numbers ~1-5% off from both outside truth and the app's own underlying statements -- money-relevant valuation inputs shown as true when wrong. Smallest fix shape: recompute eps and book_value from the already-fetched net_income_ttm/stockholders_equity/shares_outstanding instead of (or reconciled against) the raw yfinance info-dict fields, or surface a field_meta warning when they diverge beyond a tolerance.

refuter.reason: The book-value leg holds. book_value=54.361 is yfinance's raw info['bookValue'], served with field_meta status 'ok'. It disagrees with the outside value (57.0, screener) and with the app's own balance sheet (FY2026 Common Stock Equity 477,377,000 / 8,373,700 shares = 57.01). It also drags P/B (1.63-1.66 in the app vs 1.55 computed from screener). The EPS leg does not survive as a same-definition mismatch. eps is raw info['trailingEps'], and the app's own income statement shows diluted EPS about 2% below basic (FY2026 9.77 vs 9.98). The 1.4% gap between 13.69 and 13.89 fits a diluted-vs-basic difference. So EPS is a definitional difference plus a missing basis label, not a wrong value. Severity stays high on the book-value leg: a wrong, money-relevant value shown as true that feeds P/B.

title: ROE is blank and ROCE has no field at all, despite the app already holding the ingredients for a computed ROE
repro: GET http://127.0.0.1:52152/fundamentals/JUMBO -> roe:null (field_meta: status='unavailable', reason='provider did not publish this field'); no 'roce' key exists anywhere in the response schema.
evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/collected/P7_JUMBO.json:251 (roe:null), :406-412 (field_meta.roe), :259-262 (net_income_ttm, shares_outstanding present in the same payload), :1211-1219 (Stockholders Equity present via the balance route); outside cross-check docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/packs/P7_JUMBO.json:roe (screener 14.2% / BSE 33.58%, flagged as a basis-dependent SOURCE DISAGREEMENT) and roce (screener 14.6%, single clean source, no disagreement)
notes: Mechanism: net_income_ttm (116,379,000) and stockholders_equity (477,377,000, from the app's own balance-sheet call) divide to a plausible ROE (~24.4%) that the app could surface as a computed approximation with a basis caveat, but instead returns null with no computed fallback; ROCE is not modelled as a concept anywhere in the fundamentals schema, so it is unavailable even in principle. Consequence: two of the most commonly screener-checked profitability ratios for an Indian small-cap are entirely absent from the terminal, against a stated benchmark (screener.in) that has both. Smallest fix shape: add a computed ROE (net_income_ttm / latest stockholders_equity, labelled with its basis) as a fallback when the provider field is unavailable, and add an ROCE capability sourced the same way the other computed ratios (debt_to_equity, margins) already are.

refuter.reason: Confirmed. roe is only yfinance's raw returnOnEquity, with no fallback computed from net income over equity. When yfinance omits it, the field is null and labelled 'provider did not publish this field'. ROCE does not exist anywhere in the sidecar models, frontend or shared types. The outside ROE is disputed (screener 14.2% vs BSE 33.58%), so a computed fallback must state its basis, but a value exists outside the app and the screener-parity benchmark carries both ROE and ROCE (14.6%). Medium stands: the blank is labelled honestly, but it covers a core ratio.

refuter.reason: The gap is real. title: Sector/industry for NAPEROL (BSE 500298) shown as 'Basic Materials/Chemicals', the pre-Sep-2023-demerger classification, not the company's current holding-company business
repro: GET http://127.0.0.1:52152/fundamentals/NAPEROL -> sector: 'Basic Materials', industry: 'Chemicals' (field_meta status 'ok', provider yfinance, as_of 2026-09-19T09:44:05Z). BSE's own live classification for the same scrip is sector 'Financial Services', industry 'Investment Company' (ComHeader API, as_of 2026-09-22), and the company's own investor-relations page confirms the underlying fact: the Sep-2023 Composite Scheme of Arrangement demerged the chemicals-manufacturing business into NPL Chemicals Ltd and left the surviving Naperol Investments Ltd entity ('the Company') running only an investment/leasing business since 1-Apr-2022 (appointed date).
evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/collected/P8_NAPEROL.json (calls.fundamentals.body.sector, .industry, .field_meta.sector, .field_meta.industry) vs docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/packs/P8_NAPEROL.json (identity.sector.value='Financial Services', identity.industry.value='Investment Company', source https://api.bseindia.com/BseIndiaAPI/api/ComHeader/w?quotetype=EQ&scripcode=500298&seriesid=; identity.former_names note; traps[0])
notes: yfinance's classification for this ISIN was never refreshed after the 2023 corporate restructuring, so a sector-based screen, peer comparison, or an agent reasoning about 'what business is this company in' would classify a debt-free investment holding company as a chemicals manufacturer -- exactly the stale-description trap the pack's own trap #1 predicted. Smallest fix shape: for equity.region=IN symbols, prefer/overwrite yfinance sector/industry with the BSE ComHeader classification (already fetched successfully for identity fields on this same symbol), or at minimum flag sector/industry as stale when a resolved instrument has a recorded rename/scheme event.

refuter.reason: The mismatch is real. Both authoritative Indian classifiers put the scrip in Financial Services / Investment Company: BSE ComHeader per the pack, and screener.in, whose breadcrumb I re-fetched. The app instead serves yfinance's 'Basic Materials / Chemicals' as status ok, because NAPEROL is absent from the bundled india_sector_map, which the app's own pipeline builds BSE-first. Two corrections. title: Income statement / balance sheet / cash flow for Amal Ltd (BSE 506597) silently show the US bank Amalgamated Financial Corp's real financials
repro: GET http://127.0.0.1:52152/fundamentals/AMAL/income (or /balance, /cashflow) while the app's own /resolve and /fundamentals/AMAL correctly identify AMAL as BSE 506597 'Amal Ltd' (ISIN INE841D01013). evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/collected/P9_AMAL.json:547-1946 (income/balance/cashflow blocks, provider 'openbb-mcp') vs docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/collected/P19_AMAL.json:505-1904 — identical values line for line; sidecar/services/openbb_mcp_provider.py:260-262 (_normalize_symbol only upper-cases/dot-replaces, no BSE/NSE region suffix) and :463-481 (get_income_statement/get_balance_sheet/get_cash_flow send that bare symbol straight to the OpenBB MCP tool); contrast sidecar/services/yfinance_provider.py:97-135 (_yahoo_symbol DOES resolve a bare Indian ticker to '<symbol>.BO' via the bundled BSE master before querying) and :417-451 (yfinance's own get_income_statement/get_balance_sheet/get_cash_flow route through that same resolver, so a correct implementation already exists in the codebase for the fallback provider); sidecar/services/provider_registry.py:495-515 (get_income_statement/get_balance_sheet/get_cash_flow call _resolve_async with validator=None, unlike get_fundamentals at :473-483 which passes _fundamentals_screener_complete/_fundamentals_has_data — so nothing catches a wrong-entity-but-well-formed openbb-mcp result before it is served).
notes: Root cause: openbb-mcp is ranked ahead of yfinance for the income_statement/balance_sheet/cash_flow model-keys (docstring in sidecar/routers/fundamentals.py:1-11: 'Phase 3 prefers openbb-mcp'), it is queried with the bare, un-suffixed ticker, and OpenBB's own default provider resolves a bare 'AMAL' to the US company. Money-relevant data shown as true — this is exactly the class of bug the product's moat claim ('data trust') exists to prevent, and it hits the exact collision the battery slot was built to probe (manifest trap T1). Smallest fix shape: either (a) route _normalize_symbol in openbb_mcp_provider.py through the same BSE/NSE region-aware suffixing as yfinance_provider._yahoo_symbol before calling the three statement tools, or (b) give get_income_statement/get_balance_sheet/get_cash_flow in provider_registry.py an identity validator (company name / currency / share-count sanity check against the resolved instrument) the way get_fundamentals already has, so a wrong-entity openbb-mcp result triggers the yfinance fallback instead of being served.

The three statement routes take no region/exchange input (routers/fundamentals.py:177-192), the registry passes validator=None for all three (provider_registry.py:495-514, unlike get_fundamentals :473-492), and openbb-mcp sends the bare upper-cased ticker (_normalize_symbol, openbb_mcp_provider.py:260-262) to OpenBB with provider 'yfinance' (_DEFAULT_PROVIDERS :98-105), which Yahoo resolves as the US ticker AMAL. title: FII holding shows null for TTC's latest quarter in the app's own BSE-XBRL shareholding endpoint, though the same endpoint carries real values for earlier quarters and the true figure is a confirmed 0.00%
repro: GET http://127.0.0.1:52152/disclosures/shareholding?symbol=TTC -> Mar-2026 row: fii_percent: null; Mar-2025 row (same endpoint, same symbol): fii_percent: 0.48
evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/collected/S4_TTC.json:2353-2401; docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/packs/S4_TTC.json:333 (screener's own quarter-by-quarter FII series: 2.19% Dec-2024 -> 0.48% Mar-2025 -> 0.00% Sep-2025 -> 0.00% Mar-2026, an explicit decline to a real, reported zero, not an unreported field)
notes: The endpoint demonstrably CAN carry a real FII value (it does for the Mar-2025 row) so this null is not a structural 'FII is never tracked' gap -- it is a per-quarter parsing/mapping gap that happens to land on the most recent, most-viewed quarter. A naive consumer cannot distinguish this null from 'not disclosed' when the true state is 'disclosed as exactly zero'.

refuter.reason: The null is real, but the mechanism is not a per-quarter parsing or mapping gap. The Mar-2026 SEBI XBRL the app fetches has no InstitutionsForeignMember context at all: the company's filing simply omits the zero foreign category, while the Mar-2025 filing carried 0.48. parse_shp_xbrl leaves a missing category absent by documented design, so it does not fabricate a zero. The same row does make 0.00 derivable: institutions_percent 5.83 equals dii_percent 5.83. The residual is a cheap improvement (infer FII 0 when institutions equals domestic). No UI or research consumer reads fii_percent, so it is low.

title: Earnings EPS-estimate 'Std. dev.' field is a high/low-spread approximation mislabeled as a real standard deviation, and pairs with a fabricated-looking '/0' analyst count
repro: Open the Earnings Calendar panel for a symbol whose yfinance `earnings_estimate` frame lacks a `numberOfAnalysts` value (common outside large-cap US names) and inspect an upcoming report's estimate row: the EPS Estimate Grid shows 'Std. dev.: <value>' (EpsEstimateGrid.tsx:68) and the calendar table renders '<value> / 0' (EarningsCalendarPanel.tsx:364) - a real-looking dispersion figure paired with zero contributing analysts.
evidence: sidecar/services/earnings_provider.py:244-260 (`eps_stddev = (eps_high - eps_low) / 4.0` approximation, `analyst_count` defaults to 0 when yfinance omits `numberOfAnalysts`), types/earnings.ts:36-37 (field doc: 'Estimate dispersion (standard deviation of analyst forecasts)'), src/modules/earnings/EpsEstimateGrid.tsx:68 (label 'Std. dev.'), src/modules/earnings/EarningsCalendarPanel.tsx:364 (renders `stddev / analyst_count` with no provenance marker)
notes: Data-honesty gap: the code comment at earnings_provider.py:244-245 admits this is 'a coarse dispersion' approximation (high/low span assumed to be ~4 stddev under a 95% CI rule), but nothing downstream discloses that - the TS contract calls it a real standard deviation, the grid labels it plainly 'Std. dev.', and the calendar table shows it next to an analyst count that can independently be 0 while the stddev is still non-null, reading as a computed statistic backed by zero analysts. For a finance terminal whose entire moat is claimed to be data trust, an undisclosed approximation presented as a real statistic is exactly the kind of promise-vs-code gap 0.9.0 should not ship with. Smallest fix: rename the field/label to something like 'Est. range (approx.)' or add a provenance flag (e.g. `eps_estimate_stddev_is_approx: bool`) threaded from earnings_provider.py through types/earnings.ts to both UI components, and suppress or footnote the ratio when analyst_count is 0.

refuter.reason: Core defect holds and is live: both the calendar event and the estimate-detail paths set eps_estimate_stddev = (high-low)/4 unconditionally (earnings_provider.py:259-261 and :428-429; the estimate frame is never read for a real dispersion), and the TS contract (types/earnings.ts:36) and EpsEstimateGrid (EpsEstimateGrid.tsx:68 'Std. dev.') present it as a true standard deviation with no approximation flag; the range/4 rule also underestimates sigma for small analyst counts (few-analyst small/mid caps are exactly where it is shown). Corrections: (a) the calendar table header is already 'Dispersion / # analysts' (EarningsCalendarPanel.tsx:318), so only the grid label and TS doc claim 'standard deviation'; (b) the '/0 analysts' half is not reproduced - AAPL returns 27 and SIFY 1 from numberOfAnalysts, and a single-analyst range of 0 yields stddev null via the `or None`, so the stddev-with-zero-analysts pairing needs a frame lacking numberOfAnalysts while the calendar carries high!=low (possible, since analyst_count defaults to 0 rather than null, but unobserved); (c) the repro's 'common outside large-cap US names' is wrong for Indian listings - RELIANCE.NS/TCS.NS return no upcoming event at all, so the field never renders for them.

title: Brave/Mojeek keyless-search parsers are covered only by frozen fixtures — nothing detects live SERP markup drift
repro: design: sidecar/tests/test_brave_backend.py and test_mojeek_backend.py assert against saved HTML fixtures only; no scheduled job or smoke check re-fetches a live query and validates the parse.
evidence: sidecar/services/search/brave.py, mojeek.py; sidecar/tests/test_brave_backend.py, test_mojeek_backend.py; docs/redesign/verification/R7_RUN_REPORT.md:41
notes: A keyless-first product's default search tier can silently start returning zero results the moment Brave or Mojeek changes markup, with no signal until a user notices. Smallest fix: a low-frequency (e.g. daily) CI or cron smoke job that runs one real query through each parser and alerts on an empty/malformed result.

refuter.reason: It is correct that Brave and Mojeek are covered only by an inline HTML fixture (test_brave_backend.py:19,67) and that no scheduled workflow re-validates live markup (no schedule or cron in .github/workflows). The consequence is overstated: markup drift does not by itself make the default tier return zero results. DDG is the primary engine (keyless.py:53 ENGINE_CHAIN = ddg, brave, mojeek), and a zero-row parse rotates to the next engine (keyless.py:170-176). brave.py:8-13 also uses layered selectors so class drift degrades fields before rows. The real mechanism is narrower but still silent. A drifted parser returns an empty SUCCESS, which calls breaker.record_success() (keyless.py:163) and is logged only as 'no results'. The breaker never benches it and tier_status stays healthy, so the fallback is dead exactly in the DDG-throttled case it exists for. The same fixture-only gap applies to the primary DDG parser.

notes: Constitution VIII ('surfacing an honest, human unavailable — naming what would unlock it — only when every configured source has failed') and spec.md's Edge Cases (both the general list and the Pass-B list, INT-SP-51/84/91 all name this exact case) promise the SYSTEM does this, not just the agent tool leg.
